subject: general
question: India observed World No Tobacco Day on which date in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**31 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World No Tobacco Day** is observed globally every year on **31 May** to create awareness about the harmful and deadly effects of tobacco use and exposure to second-hand smoke.
 
• The initiative was first started by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** in **1987** to draw global attention to the tobacco epidemic and the preventable death and disease it causes.
 
• The **World Health Assembly** passed **Resolution WHA42.19** in **1988**, which formally called for the celebration of **World No Tobacco Day** every year on **31 May**.
 
• In **2025**, **India** continues its active participation in this global campaign, led by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**, to strengthen tobacco control measures and protect the younger generation from nicotine addiction.
 
• The day serves as a call to action, advocating for effective policies to reduce tobacco consumption and engaging stakeholders across various sectors to join the fight against the tobacco industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tobacco Control Legislation in India:**
 
 
• The **Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA)**, passed in **2003**, is the primary law that regulates the advertisement, production, and distribution of tobacco products in **India**.
 
• **Section 4** of **COTPA** prohibits smoking in **public places**, while **Section 6** prohibits the sale of tobacco products to **minors** (below **18 years** of age) and within **100 yards** of educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **Health and Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Tobacco use is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) including **lung cancer**, **cardiovascular diseases**, and **chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)**.
 
• According to the **Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS)**, **India** has one of the highest numbers of tobacco users globally, which imposes a massive economic burden due to healthcare costs and lost productivity.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **2007-08** with the aim of creating awareness and ensuring effective implementation of **COTPA** provisions.
 
• In **September 2019**, the Indian government enacted the **Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act** to ban the production, import, sale, and advertisement of **e-cigarettes** to prevent health risks to the youth.
 
 
 
• **WHO MPOWER Measures:**
 
 
• The **WHO** introduced the **MPOWER** package to help countries implement the **WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC)**.
 
• This includes **Monitoring** tobacco use, **Protecting** people from smoke, **Offering** help to quit, **Warning** about dangers, **Enforcing** bans on advertising, and **Raising** taxes on tobacco.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Statistics:** Tobacco kills more than **8 million** people each year, including an estimated **1.3 million** non-smokers who are exposed to **second-hand smoke**.
 
• **Tobacco Cultivation:** **India** is the **second-largest** producer of tobacco in the world, with states like **Andhra Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Karnataka** being the primary hubs for its cultivation.
 
• **Constitutional Provision:** **Article 47** of the **Constitution of India** directs the State to endeavor to bring about the prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health, providing a basis for tobacco control.
